title: Analytics Measurement Plans, Consent, and Cardinality Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies analytics measurement plans, consent, and cardinality?
options: Start with a decision and a versioned bounded event contract whose population, consent, and failure semantics are explicit.
questions.answer: Start with a decision and a versioned bounded event contract whose population, consent, and failure semantics are explicit.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: An increase in event count proves that more users completed the journey.
questions.explanation: Sending a unique order ID as an analytics parameter creates high cardinality and may turn product measurement into unnecessary personal or transactional tracking.

questions.prompt: What must accompany a conversion numerator?
questions.answer: A clearly defined eligible population and denominator collected under compatible semantics.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
